title: The day and night of Brahma, and two paths

verses.sa: अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः । तस्याहं सुलभः पार्थ नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, for the one whose mind is wholly on me and who remembers me constantly, I am easy to reach.
verses.angle: Easy to reach for the one-pointed yogi
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After telling Arjuna how to leave the body, Krishna steps back to describe the living path of devotion. Listen for the condition that makes him easy to reach.

body.text: Arjuna, for the one whose mind is wholly on me and who remembers me constantly, I am easy to reach. Krishna says he is easy to reach, sudhalam, for the yogi who is nitya-yuktasya, ever-joined, and whose mind is ananya-cetah, one-pointed, so that his remembrance is constant. He then says that great souls who reach him do not return to this cycle of birth.

verses.sa: मामुपेत्य पुनर्जन्म दुःखालयमशाश्वतम् । नाप्नुवन्ति महात्मानः संसिद्धिं परमां गताः ॥
verses.tr: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth.
verses.angle: Dhuhalayama: the temporary home of pain
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by naming the destination that lies beyond the cycle of birth, a place where suffering ends.

body.text: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth. The word dhuhalayama, abode of suffering, describes this world of rebirth, and the verse tells us that those who reach Krishna do not return to it. Krishna then speaks of all worlds returning to this same cycle, except for the one who reaches him.

verses.sa: आब्रह्मभुवनाल्लोकाः पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन । मामुपेत्य तु कौन्तेय पुनर्जन्म न विद्यते ॥
verses.tr: All worlds up to Brahma's realm return again, Arjuna. But having reached me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna names the highest heaven and says even that one sends beings back, yet there is one permanent way out.

body.text: All worlds up to Brahma's realm return again, Arjuna. But having reached me, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth. The word punaravartinah means returning again. Krishna uses it to name the endless cycle of birth and death, and then he offers one permanent way out. He now explains the true length of Brahma's day and night to show why even cosmic time is temporary.

verses.sa: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
verses.tr: Those who know that Brahma’s day lasts a thousand yugas, and his night lasts a thousand yugas, know day and night truly.
verses.angle: Ahah ratrividah: knowers of day and night
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the vast duration of Brahma's day and night. Listen for the word that measures this cosmic time.

body.text: Those who know that Brahma’s day lasts a thousand yugas, and his night lasts a thousand yugas, know day and night truly. The phrase ahah ratrividah literally means knowers of day and night. In this verse, the phrase ahah ratrividah refers to the people who know the true length of Brahma's day and night, which is defined by the term yugas. At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest, and at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.

verses.sa: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्त्यहरागमे । रात्र्यागमे प्रलीयन्ते तत्रैवाव्यक्तसंज्ञके ॥
verses.tr: At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest; at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes a cycle of birth and dissolution. Listen for the word that names the source from which beings arise and into which they dissolve.

body.text: At the start of Brahma's day, all beings arise from the unmanifest; at the start of Brahma's night, they dissolve back into that same unmanifest. The word is avyakta, the unmanifest. Beings arise from it and dissolve back into it, showing that this is the source of their appearance and disappearance. Krishna then says that this entire group of beings is born again and again, helplessly, at the coming of day.

verses.sa: भूतग्रामः स एवायं भूत्वा भूत्वा प्रलीयते । रात्र्यागमेऽवशः पार्थ प्रभवत्यहरागमे ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, this entire group of beings is born again and again, and is dissolved at the coming of night; at the coming of day, it rises again, helplessly.
verses.angle: avashah: helpless compulsion in the cosmic cycle
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the unmanifest and its cosmic rhythm. Now listen to what happens to all living beings caught inside that rhythm.

body.text: O Arjuna, this entire group of beings is born again and again, and is dissolved at the coming of night; at the coming of day, it rises again, helplessly. The word avashah means helplessly, under compulsion. Every being is forced to arise and dissolve again and again. They have no choice in this cycle. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: परस्तस्मात्तु भावोऽन्योऽव्यक्तोऽव्यक्तात्सनातनः । यः स सर्वेषु भूतेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति ॥
verses.tr: Beyond that unmanifest is another, eternal unmanifest. Even when all beings perish, it does not perish.
verses.angle: Beyond the unmanifest lies another eternal unmanifest
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has traced the path of every living form from birth to dissolution, and now he points to what remains when all forms vanish. Listen to how he names the imperishable.

body.text: Beyond that unmanifest is another, eternal unmanifest. Even when all beings perish, it does not perish. The verse holds two unmanifest states, and the word parastasmattu, beyond that, marks the shift from the temporary to the eternal. The unmanifest that dissolves gives way to the one that cannot be destroyed, even when all beings perish. Krishna calls this eternal unmanifest the highest goal and his supreme abode, from which there is no return.

verses.sa: अव्यक्तोऽक्षर इत्युक्तस्तमाहुः परमां गतिम् । यं प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
verses.tr: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After describing a reality beyond the changing world, Krishna turns to Arjuna. He now names the destination itself. Listen for the word that marks the end of every cycle of return.

body.text: That is called the unmanifest and the imperishable. It is the highest goal. Having reached it, one does not return. It is my supreme abode. The verse calls the destination paramam dhama, the supreme abode. It is the highest goal, and reaching it means one does not return. Krishna now explains how Arjuna can reach this supreme person through undivided devotion.

verses.sa: पुरुषः स परः पार्थ भक्त्या लभ्यस्त्वनन्यया । यस्यान्तःस्थानि भूतानि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, the supreme person is reached through undivided devotion. All beings dwell within that being, and this entire world is pervaded by that being.
verses.angle: Unanya bhakti is the path to the supreme person
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now describes the supreme person and the path to reach him. Listen to how he links the way to him with what he already is.

body.text: O Arjuna, the supreme person is reached through undivided devotion. All beings dwell within that being, and this entire world is pervaded by that being. Krishna names the supreme person as the one in whom all beings dwell, and who pervades this entire world, and then he names undivided devotion as the way to reach that very being. He now speaks of the time when yogis leave this world and the time when they return to it.

verses.sa: यत्र काले त्वनावृत्तिमावृत्तिं चैव योगिनः । प्रयाता यान्ति तं कालं वक्ष्यामि भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.tr: I will tell you of the time when yogis do not return, and the time when they do, O best of the Bharatas.
verses.angle: Anavrttim and avrttim: the two paths after death
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now shifts from the nature of the supreme being to the moment of leaving the body. Listen for the two words that mark the two paths after death.

body.text: I will tell you of the time when yogis do not return, and the time when they do, O best of the Bharatas. Notice the pair, anavrttim and avrttim. One is non-return, the other is return. Krishna promises to name the exact times that send a departed yogi down one road or the other. He begins that explanation by naming the fire, the daylight, and the bright half of the month as paths of return.

verses.sa: अग्निर्ज्योतिरहः शुक्लः षण्मासा उत्तरायणम् । तत्र प्रयाता गच्छन्ति ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदो जनाः ॥
verses.tr: Fire, daylight, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the northward course: those who depart then, knowing the supreme reality, go to the supreme reality.
verses.angle: The bright path of agni and uttarayan
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just spoken of the times when a yogi departs and returns, and now he names the very path that leads away from return.

body.text: Fire, daylight, the bright fortnight, and the six months of the northward course: those who depart then, knowing the supreme reality, go to the supreme reality. Listen to the list of light, agni, jyoti, daylight, the bright fortnight, and uttarayan, the northern course. These are not random times; they trace the bright path of the sun, the route through which the knower of Brahman departs. Krishna then names the opposite path of smoke and night, the route that leads the departing soul back to earth.

verses.sa: धूमो रात्रिस्तथा कृष्णः षण्मासा दक्षिणायनम् । तत्र चान्द्रमसं ज्योतिर्योगी प्राप्य निवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light.
verses.angle: Some routes only delay return; they do not end the cycle.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now names the opposite path, the one that leads back to birth. Listen to the sequence of images that mark it.

body.text: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light. The verse lists four images: smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern half-year. The yogi who departs there reaches lunar light and returns. The next verse states that these two paths are the eternal ways of the world, one leading to no-return, the other to return.

verses.sa: शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते । एकया यात्यनावृत्तिमन्ययाऽऽवर्तते पुनः ॥
verses.tr: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again.
verses.angle: The two eternal paths of the world
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the path of smoke and night. Now he answers what lies beyond. Listen for the two eternal roads that every soul travels.

body.text: The bright and the dark are the two eternal paths of the world. One leads to non-return; the other brings return again. The two paths are called shuklakrisne, the bright and the dark. One leads to non-return, the other brings the traveler back again, and this is true for the entire world. Krishna says the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded, so remain steadfast in yoga at all times.

verses.sa: नैते सृती पार्थ जानन्योगी मुह्यति कश्चन । तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु योगयुक्तो भवार्जुन ॥
verses.tr: O Arjuna, the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded. Therefore, remain steadfast in yoga at all times.
verses.angle: Yogi, joined in yoga, is never deluded
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown the two routes the soul takes after death. Arjuna stands frozen between them. Listen to the simple command Krishna gives.

body.text: O Arjuna, the yogi who knows these two paths is never deluded. Therefore, remain steadfast in yoga at all times. The word yogi is joined in yoga. The word deluded means confused, and the word knowing means understanding. The yogi who understands these two paths is never confused, so Krishna tells Arjuna to be joined in yoga at all times. Knowing these two paths, the yogi goes beyond the merits of the Vedas and reaches the supreme abode.

verses.sa: वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपःसु चैवदानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् । अत्येति तत्सर्वमिदं विदित्वायोगी परं स्थानमुपैति चाद्यम् ॥
verses.tr: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode.
verses.angle: atyeti: the verb that means to go beyond
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna points to a single word that marks the limit of all religious action: listen for the verb that means to go beyond.

body.text: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode. The word is atyeti, meaning goes beyond. The yogi does not merely collect the fruits of sacrifice and austerity; knowing the two paths, he passes beyond them all. Krishna now promises to reveal a secret knowledge that frees you from all that is harmful.

prev.title: What the mind holds at the very end
